critique.good: The city column is generous enough that every city name sits on one line, including المدينة المنورة, so the identifier column reads as a clean, confident stack; the city block is also clearly separated from the data block.
critique.problems: The prayer block is destroyed: 5 of 6 headers wrap (العشاء becomes 'الع' / 'شاء') and there are 11 mid-word splits, including inside the clock values themselves ('8:1' / '6', '3:3' / '8'). A prayer time broken across two lines is no longer a time — the reader cannot compare vertically at all. Rows balloon to 60px and the table grows to 418px tall, so a 7-row quick reference becomes a long scroll.
critique.cause: 112px on a column that only needs 91 leaves 49–51px for the five time columns, i.e. 28–30px of usable text against the 35–47px their headers and values require. Over-allocation to col 1 is the single cause of everything else.

critique.good: It fits the 360px box, every time value stays whole on one line, and no data cell splits mid-word. The rows read as units and the whole table is compact at 325px — this is by far the best starting point.
critique.problems: Two single-word headers break mid-word, leaving ugly orphans: المغرب renders as 'المغر' / 'ب' and العشاء as 'العشا' / 'ء'. A one-letter fragment under a header looks like a rendering bug. Row heights are also uneven (60/36 alternating), which breaks the vertical rhythm of the comparison.
critique.cause: 70px on the city column is exactly the minimum that keeps 'المدينة' (49px unbreakable) intact, so it cannot give more; that leaves 289px for five columns that need 301px. المغرب at 62 (41px text vs 47 needed) and العشاء at 56 (35 vs 41 needed) are each 6–12px short, and a shortfall on a single-word Arabic header always manifests as a mid-word break. The two wrapped cities are simply what 70px costs.

critique.good: Perfect typographic rhythm: all headers, all times and all city names on one line, uniform 36px rows, 255px total, and the five prayer columns read as one coherent parallel block with the city clearly separate. As pure typesetting it is the best of the three.
critique.problems: At 414px it overflows the 360px box by 54px, so the reader must scroll horizontally and can never see the city name and the leftmost prayer time in the same view — which defeats the purpose of a table whose whole job is cross-prayer and cross-city comparison.
critique.cause: It spends 112px on the city column (21px more than needed for one-line cities) on top of the five full-need prayer columns (56/56/59/68/62 = 301), summing to 413. The city column is the only place where fat can be trimmed.

critique.good: All six headers stay on one line, no mid-word splits, all HH:MM values are intact, and city names wrap only at spaces. The width order follows content needs: city widest, then المغرب/العشاء, with الفجر/الظهر narrowest. The prayer columns read as a coherent block.
critique.problems: The table is 372px wide and overflows the 360px box by 12px. In RTL the leftmost العشاء column is pushed outside the available area, so the last prayer is the column at risk of being clipped or requiring scroll. Several columns sit exactly at their minimum text width, so the table feels tight rather than comfortably spaced.
critique.cause: Keeping every single-word header unbroken requires 70+56+56+59+68+62=371px. The 12px excess is precisely the cost of not splitting any header; no column can be reduced without forcing a mid-word break.

critique.good: It fits inside 360px with no horizontal scroll. Time values remain intact, city names wrap only at spaces, and the city column stays readable.
critique.problems: المغرب is broken mid-word into 'المغر' plus a one-letter orphan 'ب' on a second line. That makes the header row 60px tall and breaks the one-line rhythm of the five prayer headers. The table also feels cramped because most columns are at exact minimum widths, and the header row is disproportionately tall compared with the first data row.
critique.cause: المغرب is given 56px (35px of text) although it needs 68px (47px of text). The entire 12px saving is taken from that one column, so the browser breaks the word after five letters and leaves the final letter alone.

critique.good: Every column header sits on one line, every HH:MM value sits on one line, city names wrap only at their word spaces, and the 68/62px evening pair (المغرب/العشاء) reads with the same weight as the daytime run. Rows 2–3 grow to 60px only because of the city names, which is the right reason.
critique.problems: The table is 372px wide and overflows the 360px box by 12px: the leftmost column (العشاء, the last prayer of the day) is cut off at the box edge, so its times can only be read by scrolling horizontally. Functionally the most important edge of the table is the one that is clipped.
critique.cause: Each column is already at its hard minimum — the wider of header word and time value plus 21px padding (70 for المدينة, 56 الفجر, 56 الظهر, 59 العصر, 68 المغرب, 62 العشاء). That minimum set sums to 371, so the 12px cannot be recovered from any column without splitting either a header word or a time value.

critique.good: Fits the box exactly (360px), keeps every time value intact and on one line, wraps city names only at spaces, and the header row is uniform in height so the columns still read as one parallel block.
critique.problems: المغرب is broken mid-word into «المغ» / «رب» across two lines, so one column header is visibly torn while العشاء next to it stays on one line; the evening pair therefore loses its symmetry and the reader's eye catches the break before the data.
critique.cause: To buy the missing 12px, المغرب was cut from 68 to 49px, leaving 28px of text width against a 47px word. The reclaimed space went into المدينة (72) and العصر/الظهر (60/58), which did not need it.

critique.good: Fits the box, gives the city column the most room (72px) so city names break at clean word boundaries, and keeps الظهر/المغرب generous.
critique.problems: Two mid-word splits: the العشاء header becomes «الع» / «شاء», and — far worse — the العشاء time values themselves break («٨:٢» / «٣»). Numbers that split across lines are unreadable as times, and the damage makes rows 2, 4 and 5 grow to 60px so the row rhythm turns ragged (60, 36, 60, 60, 60, 36, 36).
critique.cause: العشاء was squeezed to 48px, i.e. 27px of text for a 41px header and a ~30px value — below both thresholds. The 20px released there was spent widening المغرب to 68 and الظهر to 59, which were already comfortable.

r0A.idea: Keep the city column at full one-line width so city names never wrap, and compress the five prayer columns evenly, accepting wrapped headers and tighter time cells.

r0B.idea: Weight the prayer columns to fit HH:MM values and most headers intact, while letting city names wrap at spaces in a deliberately narrow city column.

r0C.idea: Preserve every cell on one line, including full city names and all headers, and let the reader scroll horizontally instead of splitting any Arabic word or time.

r1A.idea: Take r0C's exact per-column needs — 56/56/59/68/62 is precisely what keeps الفجر, الظهر, العصر, المغرب and العشاء whole — and cut the city column from 112 down to the 70px minimum that still keeps 'المدينة' unbroken, letting only the two long city names wrap at their space. Result: zero mid-word splits anywhere, all times on one line, uniform header band, and only 11px of overflow, which falls entirely inside the outer padding of the leftmost cell so no value is hidden. Best reading experience with a negligible, non-scrolling-in-practice cost.

r1B.idea: Keep r0B's in-box discipline but spend the same 289px smarter: move 6px from العشاء to nothing — instead swap the two evening columns so العشاء gets the 62px it needs (41px text, header intact) and المغرب takes the 56px. That removes one of the two header breaks (العشاء no longer orphans 'ء'), keeps every time value whole, and still sums to 359 with no overflow. المغرب, the widest header at 47px, is the single acceptable casualty.

r2A.idea: Retain r1A's minimal no-split widths deliberately: every prayer header and every time value stays intact, and the overflow is kept to the smallest possible 12px. The table container must scroll rather than clip so العشاء remains reachable. This is the cleanest reading if a small horizontal scroll is acceptable.

r2B.idea: Fit exactly within 359px by taking width from المغرب and redistributing it: +2px to city, +2px to الفجر/الظهر, +1px to العصر. At 49px (28px text) المغرب should break into a more balanced 'المغ' / 'رب' two-line header instead of r1B's orphan 'ب'. All other headers, city names and time values stay intact.

r2C.idea: Alternative fit: keep المغرب intact and take the needed width from العشاء instead, giving 2px back to the city column. At 48px (27px text) العشاء wraps as 'الع' / 'شاء' rather than leaving a one-letter orphan. Use this if preserving المغرب on one line is more important than keeping the leftmost header unbroken.

r3A.idea: Keep the city column and all four other time columns at their exact minimum (so المدينة, الفجر, الظهر, العصر, العشاء headers and every HH:MM value stay on one line, cities wrapping only at spaces), and take the whole 12px deficit out of المغرب alone (68→56). Result: 359px, no horizontal scroll, no clipped column, and exactly one two-line header — a single header cell pays the cost instead of a whole clipped column or a split number. Accepted trade-off: «المغرب» breaks across two lines, which is the least damaging compromise available at 359px.

r3B.idea: Deliberately return the full minimum set and let the table run 12px past the box. This is the only configuration in which nothing is damaged: all six headers one line, all thirty time values one line, city names broken only at their word spaces. The price is a constant 12px horizontal scroll; if the reader can scroll, this reads better than any 359px layout, because a torn header or a split number is a permanent defect on every row while a 12px scroll is a one-off gesture.

r3C.idea: A middle option that tests whether المغرب can be bought back cheaply: trim only 2px from المغرب (68→66) and keep everything else at minimum, giving 369px. It keeps the header on one line (47px word in 45px is still short, so this is a probe rather than a safe design) and reduces the overflow to 9px — use only if the 12px scroll of no-split-371 proves unacceptable in practice; otherwise prefer the clean 371.

contrast.idea: The instinctive 'make all columns equal' move. It starves the city column (39px of text for a 49px word, so المدينة itself breaks), breaks المغرب and العشاء headers, and simultaneously over-widens the narrow time columns — equal widths are wrong here because the columns hold different kinds of content, not interchangeable data.

understanding.purpose: A quick-reference prayer-time table for Saudi cities: one city per row, with five daily prayer times to compare across cities and across prayers.
understanding.reading: Right-to-left: the reader finds the city in the rightmost column, then scans leftward across the five prayer-time columns; vertical scanning compares the same prayer across cities, so the five time columns need a consistent rhythm.
groups: Column 1 is the row identifier and should be visually separate from the data.

Columns 2–6 form one parallel group of prayer times; they share the same value type and should read as a coherent block, with الفجر/الظهر/العصر as the daytime run and المغرب/العشاء as the evening pair.
keep_intact: HH:MM time values must never split across lines.
City names should ideally stay on one line; if not, they must wrap only at spaces between words.
Arabic header words should not be broken mid-word if avoidable.
may_wrap: Long city names such as المدينة المنورة and مكة المكرمة at word spaces.
Longer prayer headers such as المغرب and العشاء if the column budget is tight; row height can absorb a second header line.

bad.why: Squeezing المغرب to 49px (28px of text) breaks the header into المغ / رب — a mid-word break in Arabic that also destroys the letter joining, and the header row inflates to 60px for no gain.
Trades 14px from العشاء to buy back المغرب, which splits time values mid-number (٨:٢ / ٩, ٨:٣ / ٢) and adds a third 60px row: the worst of both worlds — broken data and a taller table.

The instinctive 'make all columns equal' move. It starves the city column (39px of text for a 49px word, so المدينة itself breaks), breaks المغرب and العشاء headers, and simultaneously over-widens the narrow time columns — equal widths are wrong here because the columns hold different kinds of content, not interchangeable data.

contrast.why: The instinctive 'make all columns equal' move. It starves the city column (39px of text for a 49px word, so المدينة itself breaks), breaks المغرب and العشاء headers, and simultaneously over-widens the narrow time columns — equal widths are wrong here because the columns hold different kinds of content, not interchangeable data.

final.rationale: Every column is already at its floor: 70+56+56+59+68+62 = 371px is the minimum that keeps all six headers and all six time values whole, so 360px is unreachable without a word break. Breaking an Arabic header (المغر / ب) or a clock value (٨:٢ / ٩) damages meaning and letter joining, whereas 12px of overflow only clips padding on the leading column and is recoverable by a small scroll. The r1A geometry therefore wins on the criteria that matter: one-line headers, one-line times, no mid-word splits, and the shortest table (301px) with an even 36px rhythm broken only by the two genuinely two-word city names. The fitting variants (r1B, r3A) are publishable only because their single fault is confined to one header cell.

general: When a table's minimum intact width exceeds the viewport by a few percent, prefer a small horizontal overflow over breaking words or numbers — identifiers and clock values must stay atomic.
Column width should follow content role, not symmetry: label columns and short numeric columns deserve different floors, so equal widths are almost always a fault.
A wrapped multi-word label (مكة المكرمة) is fine and expected; a broken single word is not — distinguish phrase wrapping from word splitting when judging row heights.
Buying width for one column by starving another usually just relocates the break; check that the total minimum is achievable before trading.
specific: Arabic prayer-time cells are short unbreakable tokens (35–47px); the only real slack in this table is the city column, which must still hold the 49px word المدينة.
The 360px phone viewport sits 11–12px below the intact minimum, so some compromise is forced; the choice is only about which single element absorbs it.

final.tradeoffs: Some designers would refuse any overflow inside the dashed box on principle and accept r1B/r3A's single broken header as the lesser evil; others (as here) treat a broken Arabic word or a split time as the more damaging fault and accept a 12px scroll. A third camp might drop the header row's column labels to abbreviations to buy the 12px.
final.uncertain: Whether the 12px overflow is actually scrollable in the deployed container, or silently clips the leading column's header — if it clips rather than scrolls, r1B/r3A become the safer publication choice. Also uncertain whether the one-line-width figure for المدينة (91px) reflects the longest city name, which affects how much the city column could be trimmed.

A.why: The city names wrap at word boundaries and the times scan in steady columns, but المغرب splits across two lines in the header.

B.why: The city column is too narrow: several names and the city header break within words, making rows tall and difficult to scan.

C.why: Prayer headers and times remain intact, while longer city names wrap naturally. The table fits essentially within the viewport, though the leftmost header is tight.

D.why: City names and times are readable, but المغرب breaks within the word, weakening the header row.

E.why: The rows scan clearly and city names wrap at word boundaries, but المغرب splits in the header.

F.why: The headers and times remain intact, with natural wrapping of longer city names. The leftmost column sits very close to the viewport edge.

reviews.unsure: C and F are visually very close; the screenshots make their small differences in width and viewport overflow difficult to judge precisely.

A.why: The times remain intact and the city names wrap at word boundaries, but المغرب splits across two lines in the header.

B.why: The headers and times stay on one line, while the longer city names wrap cleanly. The العشاء header is tight against the left edge.

C.why: The city column is too narrow: city names and even its header split within words, making rows much taller and harder to scan. Two prayer headers also split.

D.why: All prayer headers and times remain intact, and the longer city names wrap cleanly. The columns fit within the viewport with a compact, consistent rhythm.

E.why: The city names wrap cleanly and the times stay intact, but المغرب breaks within the word, weakening the header row.

F.why: The times remain intact and city names wrap at word boundaries, but المغرب splits across two lines in the header.

A.why: Column 1 is generous enough that city names wrap only at word boundaries, and every time stays on one line; the single flaw is the header المغرب broken mid-word into المغر/ب, which damages the header row's rhythm.

B.why: Column 1 is starved: المدينة, الرياض, المكرمة all split mid-word (المدين/ة, الريا/ض, المكر/مة) and the العشاء header breaks too, so the row-identifying column—the one a reader scans first—becomes unreadable while the time columns sit comfortably wide.

C.why: All six headers sit intact on one line (المغرب included), every time is unbroken, and the wide first column lets city names wrap only between words (مكة / المكرمة). Clear header hierarchy, calm rhythm, rows read as units.

D.why: Times and most headers are intact and column 1 works well, but المغرب is split as المغ/رب, leaving a stray fragment in the header row that breaks the clean baseline of the other five headers.

E.why: Essentially the same balance as A: comfortable first column, unbroken times, but the المغرب header is chopped into المغر/ب, an avoidable blemish on an otherwise tidy grid.

F.why: Columns are pushed to the extreme edge of the frame—the leftmost time cells run into the dashed boundary and look clipped—while the header row is tight against the border; the table reads as squeezed rather than composed.

reviewsOld.unsure: Whether layout F actually clips the العشاء digits or only abuts the dashed box; if it truly fits, F would rise to acceptable.

A.why: Fits inside the frame, all prayer times on one line, and the long city names wrap at spaces (مكة / المكرمة). Only flaw: the المغرب header breaks mid-word into "المغر" + "ب", leaving a stray letter line in the header band.

B.why: No word is broken anywhere and every time is intact, but the table runs past the pink frame on the left, so the العشاء column is clipped/scrolls; the city column also takes more space than the numeric columns need.

C.why: The city column is crushed: المدينة splits to "المدين/ة", الرياض to "الريا/ض", الدمام to "الدم/م", المنورة to "المنور/ة", and العشاء header to "العشا/ء" — the identifying column is unreadable and rows can't be scanned.

D.why: Sits inside the frame with no mid-word breaks at all: all six time columns are one line and wide enough for their headers, and the city names wrap cleanly at spaces (المدينة / المنورة, مكة / المكرمة). Balanced proportions, rows read as units.

E.why: Fits the frame and keeps times intact, but المغرب is broken into "المغ" + "رب", an orphan fragment that reads as a separate word in the header; the narrow column leaves awkward white space beneath it.

F.why: Effectively the same trade-off as A: fits the frame, times and city names intact (wrapping at spaces), but the المغرب header is split into "المغر" + "ب", the only real blemish.

reviewsOld.unsure: Each image seems scaled to its own table, so it is hard to tell exactly how far B overflows the 360px frame and whether D is exactly ≤359px or a few pixels over; A and F look nearly identical, and any small width difference between them isn't visible to me.
